title: Ci e Ne Avanzati con l'Imperativo e l'Infinito
subtitle: Combining pronouns, ci and ne with commands and infinitives, including irregular tu forms.
objectives: Attach ci, ne, and combined pronouns correctly to the informal imperative
Apply consonant doubling with the irregular tu imperatives (va', da', fa', sta', di')
Combine multiple pronouns with an infinitive after another verb

content.intro: At this level, pronoun attachment needs to work smoothly even in the trickiest combinations: an irregular tu imperative plus a pronoun, or a chain of pronouns onto an infinitive after a modal verb.
content.explanation: The apostrophized irregular tu imperatives (va', da', fa', sta', di') double the first consonant of any pronoun that attaches to them (except gli): va' + ci → vacci; da' + mi → dammi; fa' + lo → fallo; di' + gli → digli (gli never doubles). With a modal + infinitive, pronouns (including combined ones, ci, ne) can attach to the infinitive or precede the modal — both correct, but the attached form is more common in formal writing.

rules.heading: a) Consonant doubling after va'/da'/fa'/sta'/di'
rules.body:
• Vacci subito! (Go there right away!)
  • Dammi una mano. (Give me a hand.)
  • Fallo per me. (Do it for me.)
  • Digli la verità. (Tell him the truth — gli never doubles.)

rules.heading: b) Pronouns with modal + infinitive
rules.body: Voglio andarci. / Ci voglio andare. Devo dirglielo. / Glielo devo dire. (combined pronoun, both positions correct)

examples.it: Vacci tu, io sono troppo stanco.
examples.en: You go there, I'm too tired.

examples.it: Dammi il tuo numero, ti chiamo dopo.
examples.en: Give me your number, I'll call you later.
Do it right away, don't wait.

examples.it: Devo dirglielo prima che sia troppo tardi.
examples.en: I have to tell him/her before it's too late.
I don't want to talk about it anymore.

commonMistakes.why: The pronoun's first consonant doubles after va'/da'/fa'/sta' — a single c would be a spelling error here.

commonMistakes.wrong: Digli la verità → Dilli la verità
commonMistakes.why: Gli is the one pronoun that never doubles after these irregular imperatives — a genuine, memorized exception.

items.prompt: ___ subito! (Vai lì — irregular tu imperative + ci)
items.explanation: Va' + ci, with consonant doubling: vacci.

items.prompt: ___ una mano, per favore! (Dai a me — irregular tu imperative + mi)
"Tell him!" (Digli, or the wrong doubled version?)
items.explanation: Gli never doubles after these irregular imperatives.

summary: Va', da', fa', sta', di' double the first consonant of an attached pronoun — except gli, which never doubles.
With modal + infinitive, pronouns (including combined ones) can attach to the infinitive or precede the modal.
These fine points of pronoun placement are a genuine marker of fluent, C1-level control.
